images.title: Cut every part in two
images.purpose: Show that cutting every part of a bar into 2 equal pieces changes 4/5 into 8/10 while the shaded area stays exactly the same.
images.composition: Two bars of equal length, the upper cut into 5 parts with 4 shaded and the lower with every part cut in two, 10 pieces with 8 shaded, and a down arrow between them.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two bars of the same length stand one above the other. UPPER BAR: a rectangle x 100 to 1100, y 120 to 250 (1000 by 130 px), cut by 4 dark #2B2B2B vertical lines (4 px) at x 300, 500, 700 and 900 into exactly 5 equal parts of 200 px. The first 4 parts (x 100 to 900) are filled reddish purple #CC79A7; the 5th part is white. 3 px dark outline. To its right, centred at x 1300 and y 185, the label 4/5 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (88 px). MIDDLE: one thick dark arrow (6 px) pointing down at x 650 from y 275 to y 385, and to its right, starting at x 690 and centred at y 330, the text Cut every part into 2 equal pieces in dark sans-serif (36 px). LOWER BAR: a rectangle x 100 to 1100, y 400 to 530, the same size as the upper bar, with the same 4 dark vertical lines (4 px) at x 300, 500, 700 and 900, and in addition 5 thinner construction grey #6B7280 vertical lines (3 px) at x 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000, each cutting one part in half. So it has exactly 10 equal pieces of 100 px. The first 8 pieces (x 100 to 900) are filled reddish purple #CC79A7, the same shaded length as the upper bar; the last 2 pieces are white. 3 px dark outline. To its right, centred at x 1300 and y 465, the label 8/10 in dark bold (88 px). Across the bottom centre at y 680, the line 4/5 = 8/10 in dark bold (96 px), the largest text in the frame. No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
labels: Cut every part into 2 equal pieces
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
shaded lengths that differ between the two bars
any cut that does not halve each of the 5 parts, or a piece count other than 5 and 10
images.takeaway: Cutting every part into 2 equal pieces gives the same shaded part a new name: 4/5 = 8/10.
images.description: A bar of 5 equal parts with 4 shaded named 4/5, and below it the same bar with every part cut in two, 10 pieces with 8 shaded named 8/10.
images.context: Concept image for Cutting Parts into More Equal Parts. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a shape with some parts shaded, then the same shape with every part cut into more equal parts) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 5 parts with 4 shaded, then 10 pieces.
images.teaching_notes: Point at the end of the shaded length on both bars: it stops at the same place. The slip to watch: thinking more pieces means more is shaded, when only the cut lines were added.

image_decisions.why: The two bars with the same shaded length make it visible that only the cut lines were added, so the area is the same and only the name changes.
